label: Drive to conditions
title: Driving to the conditions
headline: Gravel, dust, floods and fog
intro: More than half of Namibia's roads are gravel, and the weather can change fast. Learn how to slow down and adapt before the road decides for you.

scenes.question: What share of Namibia's national road network is gravel?

lines: You're driving to a farm outside Gobabis. The tar ends and the road turns to gravel.
The limit on an untarred road outside town is {claim:na.law.speed-gravel}, but that's a maximum, not a target.

art.alt: A gravel road through dry bush in the middle of the day.

scenes.prompt: Loose gravel gives your tyres much less grip. Compare stopping distances on tar and on gravel at the same speed.

art.alt: Two bars comparing stopping distance on dry tar and on gravel, with minibus-taxi lengths for scale.

states.label: {n:80} km/h
states.caption: At {n:80} km/h: about {var:d0} m on tar, but {var:d1} m on gravel.

states.label: {n:100} km/h
states.caption: At {n:100} km/h: about {var:d0} m on tar, but {var:d1} m on gravel, about {var:taxis1} taxi lengths.

scenes.explain: About {claim:na.stat.gravel-share} of Namibia's national roads are gravel. On loose gravel your car needs much further to stop, so slow down well below the limit.

art.alt: A gravel road with dust hanging in the air.

steps.title: Slow down
steps.body: Choose a speed at which you can stop within the distance you can see.

steps.title: Leave a bigger gap
steps.body: Stay well back out of the dust of the car ahead: at least double your usual gap.

steps.title: Steer gently
steps.body: No sudden turns or hard braking. On loose stones the car can slide or roll.

steps.title: Headlights on
steps.body: Dust hides you from oncoming drivers. Lights help them see you.

lines: On gravel, drive well below the limit: you need much further to stop.
Hang back out of the dust and keep your headlights on.
Gentle steering and braking keep you on the road.

scenes.question: How deep does rushing water need to be to carry away most cars?

lines: It rained hard upstream overnight. The road dips through a riverbed, and water is running across it.
It doesn't look very deep, and the other side is close.

art.alt: Side view of a road dipping through a riverbed, with water across it and a depth post.

scenes.prompt: You can't see how deep or fast the water is, or whether the road underneath has washed away. See what different depths do.

art.alt: Side view of the crossing with the water rising against a depth post.

states.label: Ankle deep
states.caption: Fast water only {claim:int.nws.water-person} deep can knock an adult off their feet.

states.label: Knee deep
states.caption: Rushing water {claim:int.nws.water-car} deep can carry away most cars.

states.label: Thigh deep
states.caption: At {claim:int.nws.water-suv}, even SUVs and bakkies can be swept away.

scenes.explain: Rushing water only {claim:int.nws.water-car} deep can carry away most cars. Water that looks calm can still be moving fast underneath.

lines: If a road is flooded, turn around and wait. Never drive, walk or ride through.
The road under the water may already be washed away.
Check the weather and road reports before you travel in the rainy season.

scenes.question: By law, your headlights must be on whenever people and vehicles aren't clearly visible at what distance?

lines: You're driving to Swakopmund. Near the coast, fog rolls in off the sea.
On the way back inland, a dust storm blows across the road.

art.alt: A tarred road disappearing into coastal fog.

scenes.prompt: How far ahead can you see? Compare a clear day, coastal fog and a dust storm.

art.alt: A tarred road, shown in clear weather, fog and dust.

states.label: Clear
states.caption: On a clear day you can see far ahead and have time to react.

states.label: Fog
states.caption: In thick fog the road ahead disappears. Slow right down so you can stop within what you can see.

states.label: Dust
states.caption: In a dust storm, pull well off the road if you can't see, and switch your lights on so others can see you.

scenes.explain: Your headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and whenever people and vehicles aren't clearly visible at {claim:na.law.lights-150}.

questions.prompt: When may you use your fog lamps?

options.label: Only in fog, mist, dust or smoke

questions.reason: Fog lamps may only be used when visibility is poor because of snow, fog, mist, dust or smoke.

questions.prompt: In fog, which headlights help most?
questions.reason: Main beam reflects off the fog back into your eyes. Dipped headlights light the road without the glare.

lines: Slow down until you can stop within the distance you can see.
Lights on in fog and dust, dipped not main beam.
Don't overtake when you can't see. If it's too bad, pull well off and wait.
